answer: A verifiable delay function toll charges each seat fresh serial time every epoch. A public beacon fixes the seed only at epoch open, so nobody can start early. Each seat then posts 30 million modular squarings over that seed and its own key, about 20 minutes on the fastest core, checked in under a second; without it a seat cannot claim any task that epoch, from a reef bleaching survey to a wharf berth schedule. Squaring cannot be split across cores and a proof binds one key, so 400 fakes keep 400 cores busy every epoch. A server farm on a windy ridge cuts the power bill, not the clock.
